![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/b8e332d7f53868313cc589e4ce5e991d2bcce88d15613111c4d0f920b678830d.png)

Which expression gives the total finite area enclosed between the curves $x={y}^{4}$ and $x={y}^{2},$ as shown above?

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(y)={y}^{4}$ and $g(y)={y}^{2}.$ First, we find the intersections of the two curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ {y}^{4} & ={y}^{2} \\ {y}^{4}-{y}^{2} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}({y}^{2}-1) & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(y-1)(y+1) & =0 \\ y & =-1,0,1\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/8b4cbf07b9c2a6d949a58f39489889d2a3fdd4690664e530386f6f61d9aac5fd.png)

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $y\in [-1,0],$ and the right function is $g(y)$ while the left function is $f(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(g(y)-f(y))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({y}^{2}-{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $y\in [0,1],$ and the right function is $g(y)$ while the left function is $f(y).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(g(y)-f(y))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}={\int }_{-1}^{0}({y}^{2}-{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
